import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def solve(prices, split_factors):
    # Ensure inputs are pandas DataFrames
    if not isinstance(prices, pd.DataFrame) or not isinstance(split_factors, pd.DataFrame):
        raise ValueError("Both prices and split_factors must be pandas DataFrames.")
    
    # Ensure both DataFrames have the same shape and columns
    if prices.shape != split_factors.shape or not all(prices.columns == split_factors.columns):
        raise ValueError("prices and split_factors must have the same shape and columns.")
    
    # Initialize the result DataFrame with zeros
    weights = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=prices.index, columns=prices.columns)
    
    # Iterate over the DataFrame starting from the 61st row
    for t in range(60, len(prices)):
        # Calculate the compounded returns for the last 60 days
        returns = (prices.iloc[t] / prices.iloc[t - 60]) ** (1 / 60) - 1
        
        # Sort assets by their compounded returns in descending order
        sorted_indices = returns.sort_values(ascending=False).index
        
        # Assign weights to the top two assets with positive momentum
        if returns[sorted_indices[0]] > 0:
            weights.loc[t, sorted_indices[0]] = 0.5
        if returns[sorted_indices[1]] > 0:
            weights.loc[t, sorted_indices[1]] = 0.5
    
    return weights
